12:03 Local Time, 10:03 GMT, 15:33 IST: That's lunch on Day 3 and it's been a pretty good session. South Africa motored along in the first hour with both Bavuma and Rickelton scoring freely. Bangladesh took the second new ball in the 83rd over, which has proved fruitful for them. Taskin struck twice, finding edges off Mulder's and Jansen's bats, while the impressive Hasan Mahmud chipped in with the scalp of Simon Harmer. Before that, Temba Bavuma aggravated an injury and walked out retired. Will he come back to bat later on? South Africa will hope he can, especially with Ryan Rickelton looking calm and controlled, having already gone past his 2nd Test fifty. Else, Bangladesh will be sensing a chance to keep this match in balance. We'll be back at 12:40 pm for the post-lunch session..
12:23 Local Time, 10:23 GMT, 15:53 IST: Not-so-pleasing update from Telford Vice at the ground: Doesn’t seem to be raining, but the covers are coming on.

12:35 Local Time, 10:35 GMT, 16:05 IST: From South Africa's team management: "Temba Bavuma is undergoing assessment for discomfort in his right calf. He will return to bat. Keshav Maharaj has been released from the first Test and will play for the Dolphins in their first-class match against the Cobras starting on Thursday."

12:40 Local Time, 10:40 GMT, 16:10 IST: We're hearing that there's lightning around and the restart could be delayed. As I type, more covers are coming on. Telford Vice adds that a light drizzle has started at the Wanderers. The floodlights have also been switched on
12:50 Local Time, 10:50 GMT, 16:20 IST: More covers are being brought on now. The entire square has been covered. The forecast is for some heavy showers for the next couple of hours or so.
13:04 Local Time, 11:04 GMT, 16:34 IST: Good news from the Wanderers. Covers are coming off and we should have a resumption soon

13:15 Local Time, 11:15 GMT, 16:45 IST: We're hearing that there's rain around the Wanderers, some lightning as well and the covers are back in place. So the wait continues. Telford Vice with some more details: The lightning warning siren has just sounded at the adjacent Wanderers Golf Club.
Sachin Saharan: Bangladesh have played a really good game so far, and if they can win this match, it would be one of the biggest game-changing moments in their Test history.

13:39 Local Time, 11:39 GMT, 17:09 IST: There's no one out on the field at the moment, and Telford has another update for us: "And here, accompanied by rumbling thunder, comes the rain I said this morning wouldn't come. Heavy. But it tends to pass quickly." The covers are firmly in place, and we are in for a lengthy delay. Sorry, folks, we are going to have to wait a while now.

13:55 Local Time, 11:55 GMT, 17:25 IST: "Here comes the hail!" Telford updates us from Johannesburg as a hailstorm hits the ground. It's going to be a long wait before play resumes. Doesn't look like we are getting any action in this session.

14:24 Local Time, 12:24 GMT, 17:54 IST: We can see some activity out in the middle, but it's still very dark, and all the covers remain firmly in place. The groundstaff have now walked off the field, suggesting there's unlikely to be any immediate progress.
14:30 Local Time, 12:30 GMT, 18:00 IST: The scheduled Tea break is at 2:40 pm (local time), just 10 minutes away. With no sign of play resuming, we have now officially lost the entire second session.

As we wait for the weather to clear in Johannesburg, there's plenty of drama unfolding in Sharjah. Why not switch tabs and join our coverage of the second Test between Afghanistan and Zimbabwe, which is on a knife-edge? We are into the final hour, with Afghanistan needing 64 runs and Zimbabwe just two wickets away from victory. Naseer Khan Maroofkhil is putting up a tremendous fight, refusing to give in.
15:05 Local Time, 13:05 GMT, 18:35 IST: The final session should have been underway by now, but there's still no improvement in the weather.

Nadim Mahmud Nion: "Hi CB, do you have any weather updates from Joburg? Can the final session be played, or will it be washed out like the previous one?" It's still very dark, with all the covers in place and no movement on the field. The forecast had suggested an improvement from 4 pm local time, but that now looks increasingly unlikely. And even if the weather clears, we could still be waiting another hour to 90 minutes before play gets underway. Wouldn't be surprising if play is called off for the day.

Riyaadh: I'm 20 km from the ground, and it's bucketing down. No blue skies on the horizon either. And with minimal wind around, the clouds aren't moving away. I can see it's getting lighter towards the north now, but more grey clouds are building up behind. A typical summer thunderstorm in Joburg.
